newsitem.title: USA: British Airways eyeing Denver service.
newsitem.headline: British Airways eyeing Denver service.

text.p: British Airways Plc will examine in six months whether it wants to offer service to Denver, a top executive at the airline said on Wednesday.
"We are looking at the total route portfolio of the company. We're looking at the business flows," said Peter Spencer, director, Americas for British Airways.
The London-based airline, which carried 31 million passengers last year, including 25 million on international routes, is being lured by Denver officials.
But Spencer told the British American Business Association he could make no promises. The new Denver International Airport is keen to attract overseas carriers.

"Opening a new route is not a simple task," Spencer said, because an airline has to be sure there will be a good balance between leisure and business travelers on the flights. For instance, on a DC-10 model jet, a goal would be to have 20 of the 35 business seats filled, he said.
The carrier recently started offering service to Phoenix, Arizona.
